title: Paintsville woman charged with trafficking in meth | News | paintsvilleherald.com
text:
A Paintsville woman is facing charges, including trafficking in methamphetamine, after an incident on May 24.
According to an arrest citation written by Paintsville Police Officer Dustin Miller, he was approached by an individual outside the Shell gas station on Old U.S. 23 who told him there was a woman inside who appeared intoxicated.
Miller wrote that he made contact with the woman, Chelsea Bray, 35, of Depot Street, outside the store, and observed she showed signs of intoxication and stumbled, knocking over a cigarette receptacle.
Bray, the citation said, gave the officer a Social Security number, name and date of birth that were not hers.
Bray eventually admitted her identity, and it was found that she had a warrant for her arrest, the citation said.
Miller wrote that during a search of her belongings, officers found two clear baggies containing a white, crystal substance.
Bray was lodged in the Big Sandy Regional Detention Center on charges of first-degree trafficking in a controlled substance (greater than or equal to 2 grams of methamphetamine), public intoxication, identity theft and giving an officer false identifying information.
